preamble: Close back [u] is lowered to open-mid [ɔ]. In West Greenlandic, /u/ is lowered before the uvular consonants /q ʁ ɴ/ and is spelled o there: /ursuq/ 'blubber' is orsoq [ɔs.sɔq], while in uumasoq [uː.mə.sɔq] 'animal' only the /u/ before q lowers. Sources differ on how far it lowers. Wiktionary's Nuuk transcriptions write [ɔ], and Wikipedia's example ueqarpoq [ueqɑpːɔq] agrees. Wikipedia's prose, following Hagerup (2011), gives [o] or [ɔ], and its example illoqarpoq [iɬːoqɑpːɔq] has [o] before the medial q.

examples.note: Both /u/ stand before a uvular (/r/ is /ʁ/, here assimilated to the following s).
Only the final /u/, before q, is lowered; /uu/ before m stays [uː].
Wikipedia's transcription: the /u/ of final /-puq/ is [ɔ] before q.
